title: Forward-Backward Dynamic Programming for LQG Dynamic Games with Partial and Asymmetric Information
summary: We formulate and study a class of two-player zero-sum stochastic dynamic games with partial and asymmetric information. Information asymmetry introduces fundamental challenges involving \emph{belief representation} and \emph{theory of mind} issues, where agents must impute belief states and estimates of other agents to inform their own strategy. To avoid an infinite regress of higher-order beliefs amongst agents and obtain computationally implementable results, we focus on a linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) model and consider strategies with limited internal state dimension.
